title: The Transporter 2
full_review:
Much like its predecessor, "The Transporter 2" (20th Century Fox) delivers nonstop, high-octane action. And while this may be good news to fans of the original 2002 film looking for an adrenaline rush, it is bad news for anyone alarmed by the increasing slickness with which Hollywood packages video-game-style mayhem as entertainment.

Relocating the action from the French Riviera to Florida, the violence-drenched sequel once again stars Jason Statham as dapper but lethal driver-for-hire Frank Martin. As a favor for a friend, Martin -- an ex-Special Forces operative who rents himself out as a mercenary mover of shady goods -- takes a break from his usual "transporting" gig and fills in as chauffeur for a wealthy Miami family.

Before long, Martin shifts gears into avenging-angel mode when the family's young son, Jack (Hunter Clary) -- with whom he has bonded -- is kidnapped as part of a sinister plot to spread a deadly virus.

Alessandro Gassman (son of the late Italian actor Vittorio Gassman) plays Gianni, the kidnappers' ruthless ringleader, and Kate Nauta his hellcat moll, Lola, whose stripper-chic getups consist of little more than two strategically placed gun-holsters.

Gallic veteran Francois Berleand returns as French cop and confidant Tarconi, reduced here to comic relief.

While director Louis Leterrier leavens the brutality with wry humor, most of the "jokes" are underscored by cruelty, as when an exploding police helicopter that Lola shoots down provides pyrotechnic punctuation for one of her venomous wisecracks.

Statham has undeniable action-star charisma and manages to make his amoral character appealing and the parade of smash-and-crash set pieces more palatable than they deserve to be. Beyond showing off his physicality, in this go-round he also explores Martin's kinder, gentler side -- only hinted at in the first film -- through his sentimental relationship with Jack.

But make no mistake. Though Martin's tough-guy snarl is occasionally softened by flashes of humanizing inner conflict, he is much more concerned with breaking bones than searching souls, particularly his own. Though admittedly impressive, the action sequences, which include high-flying car chases and stylized melees, are so ridiculously over-the-top that even James Bond would find them implausible.

As far as mindless action flicks go, "The Transporter 2" is well-crafted, but its bogus message that carnage is cool is not one that should be transported.

The film contains pervasive consequence-free violence, disrespect for law officers, an implied sexual encounter, fleeting partial rear nudity, an instance of rough language and scattered crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
